subject: Preserve stable anti-vibration turn count across an aligned transition
description: Old schema-12 representative `parity-random-save-replays-60s-15x/traces/Savegame_Cyrdach/Profile_156/Savegame_015/replay-005-session-0001.jsonl.zst` first diverged after frame 1192 only on Rust PC108, corresponding to Original PC58: Original turned from direction 6 to 7 and selected sprite row 151, while Rust remained at direction 6 and row 150. Both engines were identical through frame 1191. Rust's in-place-transition priming helper had cleared the serialized anti-vibration `direction_count` from its stable value 2 to 0 at frame 1189 merely because the actor's current direction already equaled its then-current goal. Original `RHPositionInterface::TurnAntiVibration` computes the direction difference and returns immediately when it is zero, without writing `msbDirectionCount`; when the goal later changes from 6 to 9, a retained count of at least 2 rotates one sector on the first Turn call (`original-code/RHpositioninterface.cpp:236-284`). Commit `14bbf2ba226c21d76f971cd804113c44fd770a8b` makes Rust's transition-prime helper preserve the existing count on that exact zero-difference boundary while retaining its established positive/negative priming behavior for nonzero goals. The focused `in_place_transition` test set passes 2/2: the new regression preserves aligned count 2, changes the goal, and proves the immediate 6-to-7 turn, while the prior nonzero-goal control remains green.
